question.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx) \\ g(x) & ∼\frac{{c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{c}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{d}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be $2\pi $-periodic extensions of some functions from $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ to $x\in R$ with the Fourier series shown above. What is the $4\text{th}$ Fourier cosine coefficient of $4f(x)-g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be $2\pi $-periodic functions with Fourier series

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)), \\ g(x) & ∼\frac{{c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({c}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{d}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then for any constants $\alpha $ and $\beta $,

$$
\alpha f(x)+\beta g(x)∼\frac{\alpha {a}_{0}+\beta {c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }((\alpha {a}_{n}+\beta {c}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+(\alpha {b}_{n}+\beta {d}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).
$$

Using the linearity property of Fourier series, the corresponding Fourier coefficients of $4f(x)-g(x)$ are

- $4{a}_{0}-{c}_{0}$ for the constant coefficient,

- $4{a}_{n}-{c}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the cosine coefficients, and

- $4{b}_{n}-{d}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the sine coefficients.

Therefore, the $4$th cosine coefficient of $4f(x)-g(x)$ is

$$
4{a}_{4}-{c}_{4}.
$$
